scope_note: These playbooks translate bounded first-party role signals into practice priorities. Interview surfaces remain hypotheses until confirmed by the employer or recruiter.

playbooks.title: AI / Agent FDE

observable_signals.summary: Own discovery, scoping, build, rollout, adoption, and field feedback as one delivery chain.
candidate_proof: A workflow baseline and a deliberately scoped first release
Production rollout, adoption evidence, and a field-to-product decision

observable_signals.summary: Build production LLM artifacts such as MCP servers, sub-agents, skills, or controlled agent workflows.
candidate_proof: Tool contracts with identity, authorization, idempotency, and failure handling
A clear boundary between a design exercise and production ownership

observable_signals.summary: Treat evaluations, regression, tracing, guardrails, and the choice not to use an agent as production engineering.
candidate_proof: A sliced golden set with release gates and rollback conditions
A diagnosis that separates data, retrieval, model, tool, and adoption failures

observable_signals.summary: Leave customer teams able to operate the solution and turn repeatable field patterns into reusable capability.
candidate_proof: An operating handoff with recovery evidence
A documented decision about product, extension, template, or retained customization

interview_hypotheses: Project depth may test the path from workflow selection to production adoption.
Coding may emphasize applied integration or debugging, but the format must be confirmed.
System design may probe evaluation, tool side effects, human intervention, and rollback.
Customer scenarios may test refusal, alternatives, and evidence-based scope control.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can choose among rules, retrieval, generation, controlled workflows, and agents.
accepted_artifacts: A trade-off memo tied to workflow risk and baseline
A recorded customer explanation with a narrower alternative
readiness_evidence.boundary: Tool or framework familiarity alone does not prove workflow judgment.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can ship an end-to-end AI workflow with evaluation and release controls.
accepted_artifacts: A system diagram with data, control, and evidence flows
A versioned evaluation set and staged rollout plan
readiness_evidence.boundary: A successful demo or aggregate accuracy score is insufficient.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can control identity, authorization, retries, idempotency, and audit for tool actions.
accepted_artifacts: A tested tool executor
A threat or failure analysis covering partial execution
readiness_evidence.boundary: A tool schema without execution-state controls is insufficient.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can attribute an AI regression using fixed requests and versioned dependencies.
accepted_artifacts: A replay matrix across data, prompt, model, policy, and tool versions
A regression case added after the fix
readiness_evidence.boundary: Changing several variables at once does not establish a cause.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can connect technical delivery to user adoption and reusable product learning.
accepted_artifacts: An adoption investigation with user behavior evidence
A field-to-product memo with ownership and non-goals
readiness_evidence.boundary: Training attendance and copied customer code do not establish adoption or reuse.

limits: The sources support capability directions, not a universal AI FDE interview loop.
Protocol names and agent frameworks must not displace coding, state, permission, and rollout fundamentals.
Exercises must be labeled as exercises when the candidate has not owned a production agent.

playbooks.title: Data Platform FDE

observable_signals.summary: Build customer- and operator-specific data infrastructure that delivers high-quality data with low turnaround time.
candidate_proof: A data contract and recoverable synchronization path
An operator workflow for detecting and recovering failed deliveries

observable_signals.summary: Deliver across data processing, backend systems, infrastructure, and customer-facing operating surfaces.
candidate_proof: A user-to-data-flow architecture with explicit system ownership
A working slice that exposes status, failure, retry, and recovery

observable_signals.summary: Combine large-scale processing and distributed-system judgment with rapid, high-quality experiments.
candidate_proof: A capacity and failure model tied to measured workload
An experiment that protects downstream correctness while reducing time to learn

observable_signals.summary: Connect technical delivery to production adoption and measurable workflow impact.
candidate_proof: A migration or rollout with customer behavior evidence
A handoff and recovery exercise completed by the operating team

interview_hypotheses: Coding may emphasize SQL, Python, APIs, data transformation, or debugging.
System design may probe data contracts, state, idempotency, backfill, consistency, and operator workflows.
Project depth may test semantic changes, incidents, migration, and customer handoff.
Customer discovery may test whether the candidate can connect data quality to a real decision.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can define identity, update, deletion, schema, and ownership semantics.
accepted_artifacts: A machine-checked data contract
A change policy covering compatibility and consumer notification
readiness_evidence.boundary: A table schema without lifecycle semantics is insufficient.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can build incremental, idempotent, replayable synchronization.
accepted_artifacts: Tests for duplicates, late data, partial failure, tombstones, and replay
A reconciliation report that detects silent loss
readiness_evidence.boundary: A one-time batch import does not prove synchronization ownership.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can protect downstream decisions when data quality or semantics fail.
accepted_artifacts: A quarantine and replay workflow
An impact analysis linked to source, batch, tenant, and consumer
readiness_evidence.boundary: Task success and generic non-null checks do not prove semantic correctness.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can dual-run, reconcile, cut over, roll back, and retire a data path.
accepted_artifacts: A migration state machine and release gates
A consumer sign-off and rollback rehearsal
readiness_evidence.boundary: Moving data without moving consumers and operations is not a completed migration.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can separate reusable connector behavior from source-specific adaptation.
accepted_artifacts: A connector contract with version and compatibility rules
A decision record explaining what remains configuration or customization
readiness_evidence.boundary: Copying an integration and renaming fields is not platformization.

limits: The sample is concentrated in public technology-company roles and is not a census of data FDE hiring.
Named infrastructure products are not treated as universal requirements.
Pipeline completion must not be substituted for customer adoption or semantic correctness.

playbooks.title: Regulated AI Deployment FDE

observable_signals.summary: Build reliable agent workflows for risk, audit, and compliance environments with evaluation and regression controls.
candidate_proof: A risk-sliced evaluation and release contract
A responsibility model connecting system suggestion, human review, and final action

observable_signals.summary: Manage GenAI risk across design, development, deployment, measurement, and governance.
candidate_proof: A risk register with owners, measurement, and review dates
A staged deployment whose controls change with risk and evidence

observable_signals.summary: Address goal hijack, tool misuse, identity abuse, supply-chain risk, memory poisoning, and cascading failures.
candidate_proof: A threat model with trust boundaries and abuse paths
Tests for malicious context, unauthorized tools, and partial execution

observable_signals.summary: Keep evidence, guardrails, tracing, and human responsibility explicit in high-risk workflows.
candidate_proof: A replayable decision evidence model with retention boundaries
A human-review design that specifies timing, information, override, and escalation

interview_hypotheses: System design may probe trust boundaries, identity, evidence, approval, change control, and rollback.
Security review may probe abuse paths and whether controls remain effective after system changes.
Customer scenarios may test how the candidate preserves progress without hiding risk.
Behavioral depth may test escalation, bad-news communication, and responsibility under executive pressure.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can assign responsibility across system suggestion, professional judgment, approval, and execution.
accepted_artifacts: A responsibility and decision-rights matrix
A workflow state model showing irreversible-action gates
readiness_evidence.boundary: Adding a generic human review box does not establish effective control.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can carry authorization through retrieval, generation, tools, caches, and exports.
accepted_artifacts: An identity and policy propagation diagram
Tests for revocation, tenant isolation, and unauthorized export
readiness_evidence.boundary: Authentication at the application entry point is insufficient.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can reconstruct a consequential AI-assisted decision with versioned evidence.
accepted_artifacts: A trace linking request, identity, evidence, policy, model, tool, review, and outcome
A retention and access policy that avoids indiscriminate raw-data storage
readiness_evidence.boundary: A timestamped application log without versions and decision context is insufficient.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can expand system authority only as evidence and operational readiness improve.
accepted_artifacts: Shadow, assist, limited-action, and expanded-action gates
Explicit stop, rollback, and human escalation conditions
readiness_evidence.boundary: A single launch approval does not replace staged evidence.

readiness_evidence.claim: Can contain and investigate prompt injection or tool misuse without relying on prompt-only fixes.
accepted_artifacts: An incident timeline and preserved authorization chain
Layered fixes with adversarial regression cases
readiness_evidence.boundary: A stronger system prompt alone does not control identity or tool authority.

limits: The guidance is an engineering interview aid, not legal or compliance advice.
Controls must be adapted to the actual jurisdiction, organization, workflow, and risk owner.
Synthetic portfolio data must not be presented as customer or regulated production data.
